title: Finite limits and specified coherent square cones
statement: Use simplicial sets and finite simplicial sets (finitely many nondegenerate simplices) from [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set], and quasicategories, coherent diagrams, cones, cocones and their universal properties from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. A quasicategory $C$ has finite limits if for every finite simplicial set $K$ and diagram $F:K\to C$ there is a limiting coherent cone. This includes the empty shape. Put $S=\Delta^1\times\Delta^1$, with corners $(i,j)$ for $i,j\in\{0,1\}$. For a coherent square $t:S\to C$, its incoming boundary is the full subcomplex of $S$ on the vertices other than $(0,0)$ and its outgoing boundary is the full subcomplex on the vertices other than $(1,1)$. Define the incoming contraction $S\times\Delta^1\to S$ by $(x,y,a)\mapsto(\min(x,a),\min(y,a))$ and the outgoing contraction by $(x,y,a)\mapsto(\max(x,a),\max(y,a))$, on the monotone vertex chains of every simplex. A specified square cone is a coherent cone on the incoming boundary whose apex is $t(0,0)$ and whose entire cone cylinder is the restriction of the incoming contraction followed by $t$. A specified square cocone is a coherent cocone on the outgoing boundary whose apex is $t(1,1)$ and whose entire cocone cylinder is the restriction of the outgoing contraction followed by $t$. These are data types; limitingness or colimitingness is imposed separately, using the existing coherent universal-property predicates.
